cases.answer: In the 2023 ECG future-AF study (Baj et al.), balancing the training set with random undersampling (RUS) did not improve discrimination in any model and mainly worsened calibration (higher ICI = worse calibration). With RUS to a 0.5 event ratio, ICI was about 0.30–0.35 for XGB and LR and about 0.1–0.2 for CNN across sample sizes. For the CNN, ICI rose from 0.014 to 0.17. At the original event ratio (150,000 ECGs, no imbalance correction), XGB had the lowest ICI, 0.008 (95% CI 0.006–0.01), versus 0.014 for both CNN and LR.

cases.answer: In Gao et al.'s CCTA study, FAI (pericoronary fat attenuation index) was measured with AI-based software (Syngo.via VB30, Siemens). Pericoronary adipose tissue was defined as fat within a boundary equal to the adjacent vessel diameter, with HU from −190 to −30. Quantification was done within a 40 mm segment starting about 10 mm distal to the ostia of the LAD, LCx and RCA. In the multivariate logistic regression for MACE, FAI had an OR of 7.501 (95% CI 1.785–12.348, P<0.001). The univariate OR was 4.330 (2.712–6.859).

cases.answer: The Thai consensus requires that apparent treatment-resistant hypertension be confirmed by excluding pseudo-resistance: standardized office BP measurement, confirmation of adherence, exclusion of drug/substance-induced BP elevation, and 24-h ambulatory BP monitoring (home BP monitoring if ABPM is unavailable) to exclude white-coat effect. EMPEROR-Preserved's resistant-hypertension analysis defined resHTN from baseline SBP measurements, not ambulatory or home BP recordings as guidelines suggest. It therefore cannot exclude white-coat hypertension in some patients, and pseudo-resistance from non-adherence, incorrect baseline SBP measurement and BP-raising substances also needs consideration. Adherence was not tested toxicologically and ambulatory recordings were deemed impossible in such a large trial.

cases.answer: The Thai consensus requires four checks to exclude pseudoresistance in apparent treatment-resistant hypertension: (1) standardized office BP measurement; (2) confirmation of adherence to antihypertensive therapy; (3) exclusion of drug- or substance-induced resistant hypertension; and (4) 24-h ambulatory BP monitoring, or home BP monitoring if ABPM is unavailable, to exclude the white-coat effect. Secondary hypertension is assessed afterwards, before RH is confirmed.

cases.answer: On the external MS-AF dataset (single-lead wearable ECG, primary care), the Lorenz-plot CNN had sensitivity 0.989, specificity 0.956 and accuracy 0.967 for AF on Lorenz scattergrams. At ECG-record level (113 records), paroxysmal AF had sensitivity 1.000, specificity 0.870, accuracy 0.876; persistent AF had sensitivity 0.927, specificity 1.000, accuracy 0.973. The limitation is that the MS-AF dataset had only five paroxysmal AF patients, a low number and proportion of AF patients, which may affect the test results.

cases.answer: In the geriatric HFpEF/T2DM SGLT2i study, over six months of follow-up the oxidative stress markers Nox-2 and 8-isoprostane improved significantly. Nox-2 went from 1.24 ± 0.71 to 1.01 ± 0.04 nmol/L (p<0.0001). 8-Isoprostane went from 70.41 ± 5.67 to 65.67 ± 4.16 pg/mL (p<0.0001). Platelet activation markers also improved (sP-selectin 125.92 ± 12.84 to 101.84 ± 4.42 ng/mL; Gp-VI 60.99 ± 6.36 to 49.51 ± 5.89), but those are not oxidative-stress markers.
